title: The Rooftop Stargazer
subtitle: Sharing warm mugs of tea under the constellations while debugging life and code.
quote: We look at the stars not because they have answers, but because they remind us that questions are grand.
excerpt: Sitting on the edge of a fourteenth-floor rooftop terrace at 02:00 AM with a fellow engineer, holding steaming mugs of ginger tea and discussing why we fell in love with building software.
body:
Fourteen stories above Batam Center, the wind carries a chill you rarely feel on the ground.

My friend Aris and I sat with our legs dangling over the safety terrace edge, wrapped in oversized hoodies, holding steaming ceramic mugs of hot wedang jahe (ginger tea). Below us, the streetlights formed grids of warm amber, while the highway traced golden ribbons of light toward the ferry terminal.

Above us, the equatorial sky had cleared of monsoon clouds, revealing Orion’s belt and the faint dusting of the Pleiades cluster.

Why We Write Code

"Do you ever feel," Aris asked, steam curling from his cup into the night breeze, "that everything we build will eventually just vanish? Like, ten years from now, none of our apps will exist on anyone’s phone."

It was a fair question. Software is ephemeral. Languages evolve, platforms deprecate, and servers get decommissioned.

I pointed up toward Betelgeuse, the red supergiant star burning in Orion’s shoulder.

"The photons hitting your retina right now left that star six hundred years ago, Aris. Betelgeuse might already be gone. But the light is real right now."

I took a warm sip of spicy ginger tea. "We don't code to build monuments in stone. We code to solve someone's frustration right now. To connect two people right now. To automate a boring chore so a mother can read her child a story tonight. That's worth every late night."

Aris laughed softly and clinked his mug against mine. "To the ephemeral light, then."
